problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=xyz-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz),$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(1,0,\pi ).$

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}-\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz),$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(1,0,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}-\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xz)) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})-(0) \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot (2y) \\  & =2{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(1,0,1)} & =2(1)^{2}(0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
